bug_semantics: Velociraptor parse_evtx feeds crafted Windows EVTX BinXML into www.velocidex.com/golang/evtx. ConsumeUnit16Array and ConsumeUnit64Array (typo names, types 0x86/0x8a) take an attacker-controlled byte length, slice that many bytes, then walk with `for index < len(buffer)` calling encoding/binary LittleEndian.Uint16/Uint64 on a suffix that may have fewer than 2/8 bytes. Go panics on b[1]/b[7], crashing the client/server (CWE-193). A later clamp `if offset+size >= len { size = len-offset-1 }` forces a leftover odd byte even for in-range even lengths at EOF.
flaw_origin: The array consumers were first written on 2021-11-04 in gaddiab/evtx f20ab033e4a12bd28a64562a685fde4a97c0f077 (PR Velocidex/evtx#21 member 'Adding 5 more ValueTypes' by Gad Diab), then squash-landed on Velocidex/evtx as e6e1b58a24f996238b00eb5b473933c55489d4c1. Parent b476f139 has no ConsumeUnit16Array/ConsumeUnit64Array. Mike Cohen later added the `>=`/`-1` clamp in 4b81630e (#23, 2022-04-04). The 2026 rewrite 4b5870ad (#37) dropped the clamp and loops only while index+2/index+8 is inside the buffer.
